source.title: Clustering-based aggregate value regression
source.authors: K. Hirose; H. Matsui; Hiroki Masuda

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests error curves as cluster count changes in a linear regression method, a different model class and complexity axis from the deep-network size and epoch settings in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and test error curves for AVR-C as the number of clusters varies. Rows record test-error results bearing on the general double-descent and variance-dependence versions. Theoretical results and cited double-descent findings are not recorded as empirical rows. The reported curves are mostly qualitative; no numerical curve values are stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study reports test-error curves for a clustered linear regression method (AVR-C, ridgeless least squares) as cluster count, its complexity axis, crosses an interpolation point. This is a new model class and setting for V4. The authors identify the divergence and later descent as double descent in M = 500 simulations and in all-area electricity data.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that AVR-C shows a bias-variance trade-off indexed by cluster count. They also report double descent when a cluster's parameter count reaches the sample size (M = 500 simulations, all-area data). In all-area data the less complex (larger-k) descent performs better than the interpolation regime. A theory of double descent is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear aggregate-value regression with hierarchical clustering; varies cluster count, rather than deep-network size, training epochs, or training sample count.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported error curves differ with the number of regression models, error variance, dataset, and clustering method (TEM versus RCM). In the all-area data, RCM is less stable at small cluster counts than TEM.

fits_no_version.finding: In M = 50 simulations (no interpolation regime), larger error variance σ² makes the rise in test error at small k much steeper. The decline for k = 10–50 stays small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the classical (underparameterized) regime, noise variance amplifies the variance side of the U-shaped trade-off.

record.problems: The reported error curves are primarily qualitative plots, with no numerical curve values or uncertainty intervals stated in the text. Simulation results are repeated 100 times, but no uncertainty summary is reported. The real-data results cover the specified electricity-demand dataset and year; the paper itself notes that theoretical validation of double descent remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for every n and σ² combination: the text reports the M = 50 trends across settings and the M = 500 divergence across settings in aggregate, with no textual per-setting curve values. Other plot-only curve details are not separately transcribed; see Figures 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, and 9.

untested.parts: Whether more samples raise test error near the threshold; n is varied, but no such effect is reported.
Model classes other than clustered linear regression; whether the second descent beats the classical minimum in general.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Noise dependence of the interpolation peak (no σ² comparison is stated for M = 500); multiple peaks; disappearance under tuned regularization (ridgeless only).
Recounting complexity with an effective number of parameters.

missing.what: RCM clustering in M = 500 simulations: MSEs diverge at small cluster counts and are unstable across iterations.
The divergence point is tied to a cluster's sample size nearly equalling its number of variables; this identifies the interpolation threshold.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed to T3: this is a new model class and complexity axis with results on V4, not a different method aimed at the deep-network question. The limits_scope labels on r1, r4 and r5 are removed because those settings never reach interpolation. The V6 label is removed because r8 concerns the classical regime. Note that the second descent beats the classical minimum in only one stated setting (n = 500, σ² = 0.25); in the all-area data it is worse. V4 only requires that risk improves again past interpolation. All evidence is qualitative text plus figures, with no numeric values or uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model size and the interpolation threshold by size.
Whether increasing training sample count near an interpolation threshold raises test error; sample sizes are varied in simulations but this effect is not reported.
Deep-network and other model classes beyond AVR-C; whether the curve subsumes the classical U-shape across model classes generally.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
Label-noise dependence, multiple or split peaks, and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization; the paper varies an error variance parameter but does not establish that it drives the peak.
Re-counting complexity using an effective number of parameters and testing whether this turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: AVR-C (TEM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of clusters and measured training and test MSE.
rows.measure: Test MSE as a function of cluster count
rows.value: Clear U-shaped test-error functions across the reported settings; no second descent is stated.
rows.note: The authors describe the result across settings in aggregate; no individual curve values are stated in the text.
rows.check: With M = 50, p = 5 and n ≥ 500, the largest cluster has at most 250 parameters, below n, so the interpolation point is never reached. A U-shape here is the classical regime that V4 subsumes, not evidence against a second descent.

rows.subject: AVR-C (TEM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of clusters and measured training and test MSE.
rows.measure: Test MSE as a function of cluster count
rows.value: Test errors diverge at small cluster counts in all reported settings; the paper identifies this as a double-descent phenomenon, with near-zero training error for one cluster in the stated divergence situation.
rows.note: The authors report the trend across all M = 500 settings in aggregate; the curves themselves are shown in the figure.
rows.check: Value is acceptable. The text says test errors diverge at small k where a cluster's training error is near 0, and the authors call this double descent. The extent of the second descent per setting is visible only in Figure 3.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, simulation settings and paragraph accompanying Figure 3.

rows.subject: AVR-C (TEM)
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error across cluster counts in the stated high-dimensional simulation setting.
rows.value: Test error is minimized at k = 1; the authors state this can be lower than AVR-C with low-dimensional predictors.
rows.note: The text connects this setting to an interpolation regime with near-zero training error.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, final paragraph before Section 5: n = 500, σ² = 0.25, minimum test error at k = 1.

rows.subject: AVR-C (TEM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of clusters and measured training and test RMSE on electricity-demand data.
rows.measure: Test RMSE as a function of cluster count
rows.value: Test error is roughly U-shaped and minimized at k = 4.
rows.note: This reported curve is described as roughly U-shaped; the text does not identify an interpolation point or second descent.
rows.check: Chugoku AVR has about 63×7+25+6 parameters against 2400 training observations, so it is never overparameterized. The roughly U-shaped curve cannot show the post-interpolation regime.

rows.subject: AVR-C (RCM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of clusters and measured training and test RMSE on electricity-demand data.
rows.measure: Test RMSE as a function of cluster count
rows.value: Test error is roughly U-shaped and minimized at k = 12.
rows.note: This reported curve is described as roughly U-shaped; the text does not identify an interpolation point or second descent.
rows.check: Same as r4: no interpolation point is reached in the Chugoku data. The k = 12 minimum is a classical U-shape result.

rows.subject: AVR-C (TEM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of clusters and measured training and test RMSE on electricity-demand data.
rows.measure: Test RMSE as a function of cluster count
rows.value: The test-error curve shows a clearer double-descent phenomenon; the descent associated with a larger number of clusters performs better than the one associated with a smaller number of clusters.
rows.note: The paper also says this model performs better than the interpolation regime.

rows.subject: AVR-C (RCM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of clusters and measured training and test RMSE on electricity-demand data.
rows.measure: Test RMSE as a function of cluster count
rows.value: The test-error curve is similar to TEM but has relatively high instability when the number of clusters is small.
rows.note: The authors describe the TEM curve as smoother and clearer for double descent; they do not separately characterize the RCM curve as a clear double descent.
rows.check: Acceptable. The authors say both TEM and RCM show a better larger-k descent, but RCM is unstable at small k and its double descent is less clear than TEM's.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, Figure 7 discussion: similar curves, greater RCM instability at small k, clearer TEM double descent.

rows.subject: AVR-C (TEM)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the error variance parameter and measured test MSE over cluster counts.
rows.measure: Test MSE as a function of cluster count, compared across error-variance settings
rows.value: The text says test error is affected by σ²; as σ² increases, the test-error decrease for k = 10,...,50 is small, while the increase for k = 1,...,10 is substantial.
rows.note: This supports variance-related changes in the curve, but does not establish that variance drives the peak.
rows.check: The σ² effect is reported for M = 50, where no interpolation peak exists. It concerns the classical U-shape, not a double-descent peak, so it cannot bear on V6's claim that noise drives the peak.

relationships.condition: AVR-C with TEM clustering, M = 500 simulations and all-area electricity data (847 facilities), where cluster parameters can exceed observations
relationships.reason: Test error diverges near the near-zero-training-error point and descends again (r2, r6). At n = 500, σ² = 0.25, the overparameterized k = 1 model gives the lowest test error (r3).
relationships.display_finding: Test error diverged near zero training error and then declined, with the overparameterized k = 1 model achieving the lowest error at n = 500 and σ² = 0.25.
